OWNER DECISION applied by rev 30 (after security design review 24, docs/security/phase-18-design-review-24.md; M-26 is NOT accepted as a residual and is FIXED by design): (1) requiredIds is REMOVED from the production API. The production entry point is decide(perRealm) only. The required-realm identifier list is PRIVATE: it is built from string literals at module initialization, frozen, never exported, never read from input, and never replaceable. (2) The decision NEVER invokes a caller method or getter. Caller array elements are read only through own data-property descriptors obtained with a captured Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor; accessors, altered prototypes (Array.prototype identity is required), sparse arrays, extra own properties, symbol keys, malformed descriptors, excessive lengths and proxies (isProxy first) are refused; each index is read exactly once. No .slice, .map, .forEach, iteration protocol or spread is applied to a caller array; copies are made with captured intrinsic index loops. (3) The decision iterates ONLY the private canonical list, so an empty or reduced required set cannot arm; the canonical length is asserted to be 21 inside the decision as defence in depth. (4) decideFromSnapshot is PRIVATE and unexported; the SEAM-28 post-validation-mutation seam is reached only through a test-only loader that recompiles the same source file and calls the internal createDecider({testHooks:{exposeInternals:true}}) factory, which the product entry never exports and never calls with hooks. (5) The actual final export object is frozen: module.exports = Object.freeze({ decide }) as the LAST statement of the file (m-91 fixed; there is no earlier freeze of a later-replaced object).

DETAIL VOCABULARY DELTA (rev 30). WITHDRAWN because requiredIds is no longer an input: input-proxy:requiredIds, required-id-set-malformed, required-id-unknown, required-id-missing. No reason code, exit code, flag, environment variable, configuration key or bypass is added; page-supplied strings still never reach a detail.

ROW INVENTORY: FC8 and every other requiredIds-based row or sub-case is RE-EXPRESSED as a canonical-set or perRealm-inventory case, never deleted silently. NEW ROWS: FC16 (hostile caller-container reads, carrying the security reviewer's exact reproduction), FC17 (export-surface and canonical-list integrity) and MT-2 (oracle self-test). AUTHORITATIVE ROW COUNT BECOMES 52 ROWS: 21 (F1..F21) + 1 (F22) + 17 (FC1..FC17) + 10 (IC1..IC10) + 1 (FW-1) + 2 (MT-1, MT-2) = 52. The rev 29 total of 49 rows is superseded.

MT-1 IS REPLACED (m-93). The oracle is CONTRACT-DERIVED: docs/architecture/phase-18-rev30-patch.md section C.6 ships phase-18-rev30-expectations.json, a machine-readable expectation table whose every entry is derived from the rev 30 contract text alone. The checker reads expectations ONLY from that file and MUST ignore every harness-recorded expected* field. Coverage is total: any recorded row id or generated case class that has no entry makes the checker FAIL, never skip, and the 34 rows CONF-04 skipped, including every isProxy row, have entries. MT-2 is the self-test: the checker is run against a copy of the expectations file with deliberately wrong values and MUST report failures for exactly the mutated entries.

Zero unexpected armed:true and zero unexpected shared_worker_present stay gate conditions.

appendText.text: REV 30 (security design review 24; M-26 FIXED BY DESIGN, not accepted as a residual): the production decision API is decide(perRealm) ONLY. requiredIds MUST NOT be a parameter, a property of an input object, or readable from any caller-supplied value. The set of required realm identifiers is a PRIVATE canonical list built from string literals at module initialization, frozen, never exported and never replaceable; the decision iterates ONLY that list, so an empty or reduced required set can never arm, and the decision MUST assert that the canonical list still has 21 entries and is frozen (failure => armed:false, exit 18, shared_worker_block_unverified, detail canonical-required-set-corrupt). The decision MUST NOT invoke any caller method, getter, setter, iterator or proxy trap. Caller array elements MUST be read exactly once each through own data-property descriptors obtained from captured intrinsics; an accessor element, a malformed descriptor, a prototype other than the captured Array.prototype, a sparse index, an extra own property, a symbol key, an unreadable or excessive length, or a proxy at any accepted container boundary MUST yield armed:false, exit 18, shared_worker_block_unverified. .slice, .map, .forEach, spread and the iteration protocol MUST NOT be applied to a caller array. decideFromSnapshot and snapshotAndValidate MUST NOT be exported from the product module; the only test access is a test-only loader that recompiles the same source and uses the internal createDecider({testHooks}) factory, which the product entry never exports and never calls with hooks. The product module's LAST statement MUST be module.exports = Object.freeze({ decide }), so an attempt to replace or add an export fails or is ignored and cannot change a decision. A harness-recorded expectation is never an oracle: the conformance oracle MUST read a contract-derived machine-readable expectation table (phase-18-rev30-expectations.json, rev 30 section C.6), MUST cover every row and generated case class, and MUST FAIL rather than skip anything it does not cover.
